nodes.label: YouTube IFrame Player error 153
nodes.description: The defect this whole session exists to fix. A document loaded over a custom scheme sends no HTTP Referer header on the subframe request, and YouTube rejects such an embed with IFrame error 153. The app localises the integer as pomoMusicError153. The same frontend works in development because http://localhost:1420 is a real HTTP origin that does send a Referer. Five remedies were tried and failed, including origin and referrerpolicy.

nodes.label: Single static HTML player page on 127.0.0.1:21772
nodes.norm_label: single static html player page on 127 0 0 1 21772
nodes.description: commands/youtube_player_origin.rs: an isolated loopback HTTP server that serves a wrapper page framing the YouTube embed, so the invisible audio window has a real HTTP origin. Shipped in commit abf51d416 after a rewrite from an OS-assigned ephemeral port to a fixed port 21772 with per-connection threads via spawn_supervised.

nodes.label: HTTP response framing: headers after the terminator truncate the page
nodes.norm_label: http response framing headers after the terminator truncate the page
nodes.description: Root cause of the silent player, proven against the live server on 127.0.0.1:21772. respond() built its format string ending in the \r\n\r\n terminator, then pushed X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options after it, so those two lines became the first bytes of the HTML body. Content-Length still counted only body.len() (1078) while 1134 bytes were sent. The user agent trusts Content-Length, truncated the response mid-token at 'documen', so the inline script never completed, the iframe was never created, and the embed never loaded. Measured: body bytes sent 1134, excess truncated by UA 56.

nodes.label: Webview watchdog silent-window reload
nodes.description: Liveness comes from webview_heartbeat(label), a command the app frontend calls. should_reload_webview reloads when stale > 25s, a 60s cooldown has elapsed, and the cap is not hit. The loopback player page has no Tauri IPC by design and can never send a heartbeat, so it was reloaded every 60 seconds exactly (20:52:24, 20:53:24, 20:54:24) and the track restarted from zero each time. Fixed by exempting the youtube-player label.

nodes.label: YouTube IFrame postMessage readiness handshake and command queue
nodes.norm_label: youtube iframe postmessage readiness handshake and command queue
nodes.description: The page sends {event:'listening', id:1} to the embed after it loads, waits for onReady, then flushes queued play/pause/seekTo/setVolume. No external API script is loaded; the documented postMessage protocol alone is enough. Rust's command_script was changed to call window.__snipsetYtCommand({event:'command',func:...,args:...}) so every command goes through the queue rather than posting straight at the iframe's contentWindow.

nodes.label: Player state channel over the loopback origin
nodes.norm_label: player state channel over the loopback origin
nodes.description: The webview has no Tauri IPC, so there was no path from the embed back to the app and pomodoroMusicPlayer.ts hardcoded duration = 0 and currentTime = 0, leaving the scrubber with nothing to draw against. The fix: POST /state to the loopback server, Rust stores the last PlayerState, youtube_player_state_cmd returns it, and the frontend polls every 500ms. The embed's own infoDelivery message supplies position, duration and playerState.

nodes.label: VPS-only build discipline
nodes.description: All cargo work runs on vps-bcb, never on the desktop. The user stated it as a hard order mid-session. The -j 4 ceiling was calibrated against the local host (7.6 GiB, interactive desktop, the machine that hard-reset on 2026-09-26) and does not transfer to the 14 GiB headless VPS, so raising it required stating nproc, free -h and the documented per-job peak and getting explicit acknowledged risk acceptance; the build was restarted with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 on that basis.

nodes.label: GitHub prerelease as the artifact delivery channel
nodes.norm_label: github prerelease as the artifact delivery channel
nodes.description: The user directed the flow: bundle on the VPS, publish a GitHub release, then download from the release onto the desktop and install with the repo's existing script. Published as prerelease v0.6.848, later clobbered twice with rebuilt bundles. deploy-linux-github.sh was deliberately not used for the upload because it bumps the version and rebuilds from scratch while the bundle was already built.

nodes.label: Poisoned sccache compile artifact
nodes.description: The snipset lib test build failed with twelve nonsense errors (E0433 on every #[tauri::command]-generated symbol, E0425 on PLAYER_WINDOW_LABEL) while the source on disk was verifiably correct: 394 lines, correct md5, 5 macro attributes, balanced braces, and no error inside the module itself. A fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR compiled successfully, which confirmed the cached artifact rather than the code was at fault. touch does not help because sccache keys on content, not mtime.

nodes.label: The custom scheme is the cause, not the operating system
nodes.norm_label: the custom scheme is the cause not the operating system
nodes.description: The runbook's triage rule: a Linux user running the dev server sees the IFrame path work, and that is not a contradiction, it is the same bug from the other side. The upstream Tauri issue is labelled for Linux and macOS together, which is the same split seen here.

nodes.label: Only the invisible audio window gets a real HTTP origin so the iframe sends a Referer
nodes.norm_label: only the invisible audio window gets a real http origin so the iframe sends a referer
nodes.description: The main window keeps snipset:// and its Tauri ACL; only the player window is moved onto a real HTTP origin. Serving the whole app from loopback instead was tried earlier and broke all IPC, which is why the origin is scoped to a separate window.

nodes.label: Appending a header after the terminator sends body bytes, not a header
nodes.norm_label: appending a header after the terminator sends body bytes not a header
nodes.description: Written into the fix as a comment so it cannot recur: the user agent trusts Content-Length, truncates the response to the declared length, and cuts the page off mid-script. The new test pins sent == Content-Length and the body ending at </html>.

nodes.label: The watchdog cannot recover anything by reloading the player window
nodes.norm_label: the watchdog cannot recover anything by reloading the player window
nodes.description: The watchdog's premise is that the app's own renderer died and the UI is frozen. The player page is not the app UI, has no heartbeat, and reloading it destroyed playback while recovering nothing: it reloaded every 60 s and the track restarted each time. Exemption was chosen over hiding the window because a hidden webview risks WebKit throttling the playback it exists to serve.

nodes.label: Commands sent before the embed reports ready are dropped
nodes.norm_label: commands sent before the embed reports ready are dropped
nodes.description: Two independent reasons seeking failed: the iframe is created by the page's inline script after load, so an eval that runs first finds getElementById('yt') null and silently no-ops; and the YouTube IFrame API needs its own init handshake before playVideo or seekTo are honoured.

nodes.label: Ship the artifact through a release because the VPS link is throttled
nodes.norm_label: ship the artifact through a release because the vps link is throttled
nodes.description: Measured both ways: VPS to desktop ran at 546 B/s to 6 KB/s, a 4 MiB dd returned 98 KiB in 90 seconds, putting a 38 MB binary at roughly seven hours. The same 44.5 MB came off the GitHub CDN in 6.6 seconds. Compression did not help because the bottleneck was bandwidth, not size.

nodes.label: Publish as prerelease so an unverified fix stays out of every user's updater
nodes.norm_label: publish as prerelease so an unverified fix stays out of every user's updater
nodes.description: v0.6.848 would have become Latest and been offered to every user by the auto-updater, with the YouTube fix still unverified live: all prior native probes were muted, and unmuted autoplay in a never-focused webview was the open risk. A prerelease stays downloadable and is one gh release edit away from promotion.

nodes.label: A fresh target directory is what separates a bad cache from bad source
nodes.norm_label: a fresh target directory is what separates a bad cache from bad source
nodes.description: The source had already been proven correct by md5, line count, macro count and brace balance, so the errors were judged to be at the artifact layer rather than the source. Building into a clean CARGO_TARGET_DIR on the disk-backed filesystem forced a real compile and cleared the twelve errors, confirming the cache was poisoned. It was also the move that exposed the genuine test failures that were hidden behind them.
